proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (entitlement) to alienate, destroy, or fundamentally alter a thing. In Roman-law property theory it is one of the three classical incidents of dominium (alongside usus and fructus). As a legal entitlement that a property-holder bears, it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in its bearer (the dominus/owner), is externally grounded in the legal-institutional order, and is realised in acts of alienation or destruction. It is a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class, which is already typed as BFO_0000023.

entities.label: Dominium
entities.rationale: Dominium (full Roman-law ownership) is the aggregate bundle of property rights (usus, fructus, abusus) that a person bears with respect to a thing. It is typed as a Role (BFO_0000023 via working:LegalRight) because it is an externally grounded, specifically dependent continuant inhering in the owner. Minting it enables the part-of relation to Abusus and other incidents.

entities.label: ActOfAlienation
entities.rationale: Abusus is realised in processes of alienating, destroying, or fundamentally altering the property. ActOfAlienation (Process, BFO_0000015) captures this realisation target so that the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation from Abusus to this process class can be asserted.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific species of legal right; LegalRight (BFO_0000023) is the existing proximate parent class.

Abusus is a component (part) of the bundle of rights constituting Dominium; representing this as a subClassOf restriction on BFO_0000050 (part of) Dominium captures the mereological structure of the property bundle. Note: this should be expressed as an OWL subClassOf restriction 'part of some Dominium' rather than a bare subClassOf Dominium.
Dominium is the full ownership right, a species of LegalRight.
Abusus (as a realizable) is realized in instances of ActOfAlienation.

open_questions: Should Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right of fruit/income) also be minted as sibling classes under Dominium for completeness of the Roman property bundle?

Is Abusus best treated as a class (a kind of right that many owners can bear) or as an individual role-instance borne by a specific owner? The current proposal treats it as a class; if a specific historical or doctrinal instance is intended, it should be an individual.

Should ActOfAlienation also encompass destruction of the thing (abusus in the strictest sense includes ius abutendi)? If so, a broader class 'ActOfAbusus' covering alienation, consumption, and destruction might be preferable.
Should Dominium be modeled as the mereological sum of Abusus, Usus, and Fructus via an OWL 'has part some' restriction, or is a looser association sufficient?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus is the Roman-law incident of ownership entitling the dominus to alienate, consume, or destroy the res. In BFO terms it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a material entity (the owner) and is externally grounded in legal-institutional recognition, making Role (BFO_0000023) the correct type. Because the working ontology already contains working:LegalRight (typed BFO_0000023), Abusus is introduced as a subclass of it. Three entities are proposed: Abusus itself, Dominium (the encompassing ownership bundle of which Abusus is a part), and ActOfAlienation (the process class in which Abusus is realised). Key relations asserted are: Abusus rdfs:subClassOf LegalRight; Dominium rdfs:subClassOf LegalRight; Abusus BFO_0000050 (part of) Dominium; and Abusus BFO_0000054 (realized in) ActOfAlienation. Open questions concern sibling rights Usus and Fructus, individual vs. class treatment, and the scope of the realisation process.
